coverage.positions_by_source: PG219 has 360; this packet supplies the remaining 540. The first total counts each new prefix assignment once.

perfect: The redoubled form starts with retroflex ṇ in praṇanāma. The following radical n is dental. Where the copy disappears, the first segment of nemuḥ itself is targeted, giving praṇemuḥ. The two initial n segments of nanāma are not globally rewritten. The curādi includes both boundary choices before kṛ/bhū; the prefix belongs to the primary lexical action.
aorist: Put the augment after the prefix; on the single pari request i+a becomes ya. The m-final root takes sak and iṭ in P under 7.2.73 and has anusvāra before s. The short-vowel paryaṇaṃsīt matches Mallinātha and both dictionaries. The GRETIL verse has ā between y and ṇ. It is retained as a distinct textual observation without assigning another preverb by conjecture.

textual_observations.sense: The elephant strikes sideways with a tusk. The printed commentary names both sak and iṭ and the prohibition of strengthening by 7.2.4.

other_moods: luṭ keeps the periphrastic-future base, e.g. praṇantā. The letter n which follows ṇa in this form belongs to m before the dental; the lexical prefix selects the initial only. The paired class-one dances preserve both luṅ grades; the curādi keeps initial n and the redoubled nīnaṭ.
